August 23, 2026

Appeals Department  
Anthem Blue Cross Blue Shield  
New Hampshire

Re: Rowan Brooks  
Member ID: W579327479  
Requested procedure: Shoulder arthroscopic capsulorrhaphy/instability repair  
CPT 29806  
Reference number: POC-D47F9A88CC-69885

Dear Appeals Reviewer:

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for CPT 29806. The denial states that the submitted imaging findings do not support medical necessity. The records establish recurrent traumatic anterior shoulder instability, a structural Bankart lesion, and failure of substantial conservative treatment. I respectfully request reversal of the denial and authorization for the requested procedure.

The clinical records document the following:

- Twelve months of recurrent shoulder-instability episodes with apprehension.
- Three anterior shoulder dislocations since symptoms began, including a recent dislocation requiring reduction in the emergency department.
- Persistent functional impairment, including avoidance of overhead reaching and inability to return to work involving lifting.
- Positive apprehension and relocation tests.
- Increased anterior translation on load-and-shift examination.
- Full strength, with no evidence that weakness or an untreated rotator-cuff problem is the source of the instability.
- Ten weeks of supervised physical therapy from April 16, 2026, through June 25, 2026, totaling 20 visits, focused on rotator-cuff and scapular-stabilizer strengthening and activity modification.
- NSAID use for six months during flares.
- A July 29, 2026 MR arthrogram showing an anteroinferior labral tear consistent with a Bankart lesion, a small Hill-Sachs lesion, and less than 10 percent glenoid bone loss.
- An intact rotator cuff.
- No active infection, untreated substance-use condition, or other documented contraindication. The patient is a nonsmoker with a BMI of 29.

The imaging directly supports the requested instability repair. The MR arthrogram identifies the structural anteroinferior labral injury responsible for recurrent anterior instability. The associated Hill-Sachs lesion is consistent with prior anterior dislocation. The limited glenoid bone loss and intact rotator cuff further support arthroscopic stabilization as the appropriate procedure rather than treatment directed at substantial bone loss or rotator-cuff disease.

The clinical examination and history corroborate the imaging. The patient has had three anterior dislocations, persistent apprehension, positive apprehension and relocation testing, and increased anterior translation on load-and-shift testing. These findings demonstrate symptomatic glenohumeral instability that interferes with ordinary activities and work.

The patient has also completed a substantial course of nonoperative management. Physical therapy was completed for 10 weeks with 20 visits, together with activity modification and six months of NSAID use during flares. The continued dislocations and inability to resume lifting work show that conservative treatment has not adequately controlled the condition. In addition, the patient has experienced multiple dislocations, including one requiring emergency-department reduction.

I have not quoted a governing Anthem policy because the denial notice does not identify the policy title, policy number, or clinical-review criteria applied. A publicly available Carelon joint-surgery guideline contains criteria addressing recurrent dislocation or subluxation, functional symptoms, examination findings of instability, and conservative treatment, but the public materials do not establish that this was the exact guideline used for this denial. Under either that publicly available framework or ordinary medical-necessity review, the submitted records address the relevant clinical issues. Please identify the exact criteria used in this case and provide the complete clinical rationale if Anthem continues to rely on a different standard.

Please overturn the denial and authorize CPT 29806. If the denial is not overturned, please provide a detailed explanation addressing each of the following:

1. Which specific imaging finding was considered insufficient;
2. Why the documented Bankart lesion and Hill-Sachs lesion do not support stabilization;
3. How the three documented anterior dislocations, emergency reduction, positive instability tests, and functional limitations were considered;
4. How the completed physical therapy and medication treatment were considered; and
5. The title, policy number, version or effective date, and complete criteria applied to this request.

Please associate this appeal with reference number POC-D47F9A88CC-69885 and provide written confirmation of receipt.

Sincerely,

Rowan Brooks  
Member ID: W579327479
